display.title: Bubby Chaya Malka's Yiddish Stories: Nine Tales Before Pesach
display.summary_short: A grandmother's full home recording of nine Yiddish stories for her grandchildren before Pesach, from the Baal Shem Tov and the bear to Eliyahu HaNavi's cup.
display.summary_long: The complete home recording in which Bubby Chaya Malka tells her grandchildren stories in Yiddish in the weeks before Pesach. The young Baal Shem Tov, who fears only Hashem, chases off a man dressed as a bear so the cheder children can sing on their way to shul. Rashi's poor father throws a diamond into the sea rather than let it adorn an idol and is promised a son who will light up the world with Torah. After a warm word about being good children, she tells of a diamond found in a fish bought for Shabbos; of an old man whose Seder guests sing 'Dayeinu' and so reveal who stole the king's ring; and of a cheder boy whose game of 'trial' saves a falsely accused Jew. Rabbi Meir Baal HaNess keeps Shabbos alone in the desert, guarded by a lion. Chana prays for a child, and Shmuel HaNavi hears Hashem's call. Eliyahu HaNavi gives a field worker seven good years, and finally visits the Seder of a poor family whose mother would not sell his cup.
display.lesson: Trust Hashem and fear nothing else; honor Shabbos and Yom Tov, help the poor, and be good children who make their parents happy.

advisories.note: A Jew is falsely accused and jailed, and a mob comes to the trial with axes and torches ready to attack the Jews; a wicked minister urges harsh decrees.
A man dressed as a bear frightens children and is beaten off; Rabbi Meir is left alone in a desert where a lion approaches him.
Poor families with nothing for Yom Tov; a father storms out in despair before Eliyahu HaNavi helps.

segments.title: The Baal Shem Tov and the bear
segments.summary: The young Baal Shem Tov, who fears only Hashem, drives off a cruel man dressed as a bear so the cheder children can keep singing on the way to shul.

segments.title: Rashi's father and the diamond
segments.summary: Rashi's poor father throws a precious diamond into the sea rather than sell it to decorate an idol, and is promised a son who will light up the world with Torah.

segments.title: Be good children
segments.summary: The grandmother tells the children that obeying parents and helping at home makes the family happy, praising each grandchild.

segments.title: The diamond in the fish
segments.summary: A rich man hides his fortune in a diamond in his hat; a fish swallows it, and Yosef, who always buys the best fish for Shabbos, finds it.

segments.title: Dayeinu: the old man and the king's ring
segments.summary: An old man who provides Pesach for the poor promises to find the king's lost ring; at his Seder the king hears 'Dayeinu' and finds the thief.

segments.title: The butcher, the storekeeper and the boy judge
segments.summary: A Jewish storekeeper is falsely accused of theft, and a cheder boy's test with hot water proves the truth.

segments.title: Rabbi Meir Baal HaNess and the lion
segments.summary: Left alone in the desert because he will not travel on Shabbos, Rabbi Meir is guarded by a lion that carries him back to the caravan.

segments.title: Chana and Shmuel HaNavi
segments.summary: Chana prays for a child, brings Shmuel to Eli HaKohen, and Shmuel hears Hashem's call at night and becomes a navi.

segments.title: Eliyahu HaNavi and the seven good years
segments.summary: A field worker's wife chooses seven good years now and writes down every mitzvah done with Eliyahu's blessed coin, so they may keep it.

segments.title: Eliyahu HaNavi's cup
segments.summary: A poor mother will not sell her family's heirloom cup; an old man's two dollars keep returning until the house is ready, and Eliyahu blesses the home at the Seder.

relations.note: Contains 'Eliyohu Hanovie and the Coin' (audio fingerprint).

quality.notes: The complete recording: 'Bubby Chaya Malka 1' and '2' are its two halves, split mid-story. About 19 seconds of quiet lead-in. American Yiddish with English loanwords.
